newsitem.title: USA: Pacific, Enova seek FERC disclaimer.
newsitem.headline: Pacific, Enova seek FERC disclaimer.

text.p: Pacific Enterprises and Enova Corp asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to refrain from reviewing the utilities' merger plans, a spokesman for Pacific Enterprises confirmed Monday.
"We don't believe this merger fits the description" of FERC jurisdiction as detailed in the Federal Powers Act, said Pacific Enterprises spokesman Mike Mizrahi.

He explained that Enova, an electric power utility through subsidiary San Diego Gas and Electric Co, is under FERC jurisdiction, but Pacific Enterprises, which is primarily a natural gas utility via its Southern California Gas unit, does not fall under this category.
"Under the Federal Powers Act, FERC does not have jurisdiciton even over two natural gas utilities merging," Mizrahi said.

"There will be significant regulatory scrutiny of this deal," which must be reviewed by the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Department of Justice and/or the Federal Trade Commission as well as the California Public Utilities Commission, he added.
Intervenors have 15 days to respond to the utilities' filing, but there are no defined time limits for a FERC response.

Pacific Enterprises and Enova, which have nearly contiguous southern California service territories, announced in early October plans to merge in order to take advantage of growing competitive opportunties in both gas and electricity businesses.
